name: Blackvein
region_detail: Narrow creek valley in the southern foothills of the northern frontier mountains, accessible from northern Cador by mountain roads.
site_type: settlement | Inhabited locations | Mining town; administrative seat of the Marquisate of Blackvein.
history: An independent prospecting camp grew around discoveries of silver-bearing ore in dark seams of stone. A claims registry, elected sheriff, and trading grounds developed before formal Cadorian authority. Migration increased after the War of Broken Banners, and Aldric Voss selected the town as his seat following the Edict of the East in 3E-991.
current_state: In 3E-992 Blackvein is a rapidly growing mining center. Voss is formalizing mineral claims, taxation, and law enforcement, provoking resentment among independent prospectors and peoples with older territorial rights. Mining and assay businesses depend on secure mountain roads and supply shipments. Inexpensive metalwork entering surface markets threatens local commercial interests.
inhabitants: Prospectors, miners, industrial laborers, merchants, teamsters, officials, Iron Spurs, and visiting members of the Blackpick, Cinderhook, Karrathi, and Highcairn communities.
danger_level: Low ordinarily in established streets; localized industrial hazards, disputes, and criminal activity. Surrounding mines and wilderness vary in danger.
points_of_interest:
Claim Street; Old Camp and the First Stake; Stampyards; Upper Slope and Iron Spurs headquarters; Diggings; Claims Hall; Ore Exchange; Ironmark Assay & Trust; Black Lantern; Crooked Pick; Overland Yard; Hewer’s Rest; sheriff’s office.

Unresolved elements: Exact map hex; local street plan and individual building layouts; opening job and rumor selections; current outcomes of commercial and territorial disputes.
discovery: Narrow creek valley in the southern foothills of the northern frontier mountains, accessible from northern Cador by mountain roads. Known throughout Cador and the frontier. Mountain roads and freight connections from Redvale and Thornhollow provide established approaches.
